topic.examWeightHint: An early question worth about 5 to 7 marks. Summer 2025 ran it as Q2 at Higher and Q6 at Foundation: a graph of the uterus lining over 28 days, then [1] each for the days of menstruation, the day of ovulation and what happens to the lining after day 28. The Foundation paper also gave [2] for naming the two hormones and [5] for a table on secondary sexual characteristics.
mustMemorise: Testosterone comes from the testes; oestrogen comes from the ovaries
Menstruation: days 1 to 5. Ovulation: about day 14
Day 1 is the first day of bleeding
Oestrogen repairs and thickens the lining; progesterone maintains it
Fertilisation is most likely around ovulation
In a cycle that is not 28 days, ovulation is about 14 days before the end

note.subject: science

Oestrogen repairs and thickens the lining; progesterone maintains it

mustBeAbleTo: Name testosterone and oestrogen, and the organ that makes each
Give secondary sexual characteristics caused by each hormone
State that menstruation is days 1 to 5 and that ovulation is about day 14
Say that day 1 is the first day of bleeding
State that oestrogen repairs and thickens the lining, and that progesterone maintains it
Spell progesterone so that it is recognisable
Say when fertilisation is most likely, and why
Read a thickness or a day off the cycle graph to within half a small square
Describe how a curve changes over a stated span, giving the direction and a quoted day
Work out the day of ovulation in a cycle that is not 28 days long
sheet.howExamined: B2, 1 hour 15 minutes: 70 marks at Foundation, 80 at Higher, calculator allowed. This is an early question worth about 5 to 7 marks, usually opened by a graph of the thickness of the uterus lining over 28 days: between which days does menstruation occur [1], on which day is ovulation [1], what happens to the lining after day 28 [1], then the hormones themselves. Summer 2025 ran it as Q2 at Higher and Q6 at Foundation, with a five-mark table on secondary sexual characteristics on the Foundation paper.
traps: Reaching for any hormone you can name — testosterone, auxin, ADH — when progesterone is the one wanted, and then spelling it so loosely that it cannot be recognised (Summer 2025 B2 Foundation Q2)
Saying the lining thickens after day 28 when no fertilisation has happened: on Summer 2025 B2 Foundation Q6 the mark went to answers saying it became thinner or broke down
Swapping the roles: progesterone thickening the lining, oestrogen maintaining it
Treating day 1 as the day bleeding ends
Assuming ovulation is always day 14, even when the cycle is longer
Reading the height of one hormone curve against another when the axis has no scale
Subtracting a graph reading the wrong way round, so an increase comes out negative

steps.working: Read day 5: the lining is 1.0 mm.
steps.decision: Go up from the day on the axis until you meet the curve, then straight across. Write the value down before you look for the second one.

steps.working: Read day 24: the lining is 12.0 mm.
steps.decision: Same method, same curve. Half a small square either way is inside the tolerance.

options: Because a reading is only ever as good as half the smallest square on the grid
Because the graph is drawn to no scale at all
Because the examiner accepts any answer near the curve
whyMenu.explain: A printed grid can only be read to about half a small square. That is the tolerance every graph-reading mark carries.

steps.decision: Later value minus earlier value, so an increase comes out positive. The other way round gives a negative number, which is the commonest slip here.

workedExamples.stem: A woman's menstrual cycle lasts 31 days. Ovulation happens about 14 days before the end of a cycle. On about which day of her cycle does she ovulate? [2]

steps.working: Notice that the cycle is not 28 days long, so day 14 is not the answer.
steps.decision: The fourteen days are counted back from the END of the cycle, not forwards from day 1. That is the whole idea being tested.
Subtract the fourteen days from the length of the cycle.

steps.working: So she ovulates on about day 17.
steps.decision: Check it is sensible: a longer cycle should ovulate later than day 14, and 17 is later.

twin.stem: A different woman's cycle lasts 26 days. On about which day does she ovulate?

items.stem: Before we start, three things you have already met. Which organ releases an ovum?
items.skill: Recall the female reproductive system (previous topic)

options.feedback: The ovary. It makes ova and, as you are about to see, a hormone as well.
The oviduct carries the ovum after it has been released.
The uterus is where an embryo would implant.
The cervix is the ring of muscle at the base of the uterus.

options.text: a chemical messenger carried in the blood
options.feedback: A chemical messenger, made by a gland and carried in the blood to the organ it affects.
A hormone is a chemical, not a cell.
Nerves carry impulses; hormones travel in the blood and act more slowly.
Enzymes are catalysts. Hormones carry messages.

items.stem: A graph has days along the bottom and thickness up the side. Where do you read the thickness on day 12?
items.skill: Read a value off a line graph

options.text: go up from day 12 to the line, then straight across to the side axis
options.feedback: Up to the line, then across. That is the method every reading in this lesson uses.

options.text: read the number 12 off the side axis
options.feedback: 12 is the day. The thickness is a different quantity on a different axis.

options.text: read the highest point of the line
options.feedback: That would answer a different question — where the line peaks.

options.text: find where the line crosses the bottom axis
options.feedback: That is where the thickness would be zero.

items.stem: Which hormone repairs and thickens the lining of the uterus?

options.feedback: Oestrogen builds the lining back up after menstruation.
Progesterone maintains the lining once it is thick.
Testosterone acts on male secondary sexual characteristics.
ADH controls water in the kidney and belongs to B1.

items.stem: Which hormone maintains the lining of the uterus in the second half of the cycle?

options.feedback: Progesterone keeps the lining thick and ready.
Oestrogen built the lining; maintaining it is the other hormone's job.
Testosterone is made in the testes.
Auxin is a plant hormone. It was one of the answers examiners saw on this question.

items.stem: Between which days does menstruation usually occur in a 28-day cycle?

options.feedback: Days 1 to 5. Day 1 is the first day of bleeding.
By day 5 menstruation is finishing and oestrogen is starting to rebuild the lining.
Day 14 is ovulation, two weeks away from menstruation.
At the end of the cycle the lining is still being maintained.

items.stem: On which day of a 28-day cycle does ovulation usually happen?

options.feedback: About day 14, halfway through a 28-day cycle.
Day 1 is the first day of menstruation.
Day 5 is the end of menstruation.
That counts fourteen days on from the end of menstruation. Count from day 1.

items.stem: A woman's cycle lasts 31 days. Ovulation is about 14 days before the end of a cycle. On about which day does she ovulate?
items.skill: Apply the rule to a cycle that is not 28 days

options.feedback: 31 − 14 = 17. Count back from the end.
Day 14 is right only for a 28-day cycle.
That halves the cycle. Ovulation is a fixed number of days before the end, not at the midpoint.
That counts fourteen days on from the end of menstruation.

items.stem: What happens to the lining of the uterus at the end of a cycle in which no fertilisation has happened?

options.text: it breaks down and is lost
options.feedback: Progesterone falls, so the lining is no longer maintained and it breaks down.
It thickens in the first half of the cycle. At the end, without fertilisation, it is lost.

options.text: it stays exactly as it is
options.feedback: It stays thick only while progesterone keeps it there.

options.text: it is absorbed back into the blood
options.feedback: It is shed, which is what menstruation is.

context.setting: Naming the two sex hormones and the organs that make them

hints: It begins with the same four letters as the organ that makes it.
parts.stem: Name the sex hormone produced by the testes.

scheme.for: testosterone

parts.workedSolution: Testosterone.

hints: It is the hormone that repairs and thickens the uterus lining.

commonErrors.feedback: Auxin is a plant hormone and ADH and insulin belong to B1. The ovaries make oestrogen — the Summer 2025 report lists all of these as answers it saw here.

parts.stem: Name the sex hormone produced by the ovaries.

scheme.for: oestrogen

parts.workedSolution: Oestrogen.

hints: Oestrogen builds the lining; a different hormone keeps it there.

commonErrors.feedback: Oestrogen repairs and thickens the lining in the first half of the cycle. The hormone that maintains it afterwards is progesterone.

parts.stem: Name the hormone that maintains the lining of the uterus in the second half of the menstrual cycle.

scheme.for: progesterone
scheme.examinerNote: The Summer 2025 report notes that the spelling of progesterone was very varied. Near-identical hormone names must be exactly right.

parts.workedSolution: Progesterone.

indicativeContent.point: menstruation happens on days 1 to 5, when the lining of the uterus breaks down and is lost
oestrogen, made in the ovaries, repairs and thickens the lining after menstruation
ovulation happens at about day 14, when an ovum is released from an ovary
fertilisation is most likely around the time of ovulation
progesterone maintains the thickened lining through the second half of the cycle
if the ovum is fertilised, the embryo implants in the maintained lining
if it is not fertilised, progesterone falls, the lining breaks down and the next cycle begins at day 1

scheme.for: banded: count the indicative points present, then place within the band on the quality of written communication — Band A [5]-[6] five or six points, Band B [3]-[4] three or four, Band C [1]-[2] one or two, [0] response not worthy of credit
scheme.examinerNote: Two losses to watch for. The first is the pair of hormones swapped: oestrogen repairs and thickens, progesterone maintains, and an answer with those the wrong way round caps at Band C however well it is written. The second is the spelling of progesterone, which the Summer 2025 report describes as very varied; the word is a key word, so it has to be recognisable. Capital letters and full stops are part of the within-band judgement.

parts.workedSolution: The cycle begins on day 1, the first day of bleeding. From day 1 to about day 5 the lining of the uterus breaks down and is lost; this is menstruation. Once it has finished, oestrogen made in the ovaries repairs the lining and thickens it again, ready to receive an embryo. At about day 14 ovulation happens: an ovum is released from an ovary into the oviduct, and fertilisation is most likely around this time. Through the second half of the cycle progesterone maintains the thickened lining. If the ovum has been fertilised, the ball of cells implants in that lining and the pregnancy continues. If it has not, the level of progesterone falls, the lining is no longer maintained, it breaks down, and day 1 of the next cycle begins.

Niamh is asked: 'A woman's menstrual cycle lasts 31 days. Ovulation happens about 14 days before the end of a cycle. Calculate the day she is likely to ovulate. [2]'
Her working:

menstruation ends on day 5, so count on from there
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 1 quotes the rule correctly. Line 2 then counts from the wrong place: the 14 days are counted back from the END of the cycle, not on from the end of menstruation. The end of menstruation has nothing to do with it.
correction: ovulation is about 14 days from the end
the cycle is 31 days long, so count back from day 31
findTheMistake.feedback: One mark of the two: the rule in line 1 is right, and a scheme that gives a mark for the method would credit it. prompts.prompt: Name the two sex hormones the specification lists, and the organ that makes each one.
prompts.answer: Testosterone, made in the testes, and oestrogen, made in the ovaries.

prompts.prompt: What does oestrogen do in the menstrual cycle, and what does progesterone do?
prompts.answer: Oestrogen repairs and thickens the lining of the uterus. Progesterone maintains that lining through the second half of the cycle.

prompts.prompt: Menstruation happens on days ___ to ___ of a 28-day cycle, and ovulation happens at about day ___.
prompts.answer: Menstruation happens on days 1 to 5, and ovulation happens at about day 14.

prompts.prompt: Day 1 of the menstrual cycle is which day exactly?
prompts.answer: Day 1 is the first day of bleeding, not the day the bleeding ends.

prompts.prompt: A cycle lasts 32 days. Ovulation is about 14 days before the end of a cycle. On about which day does ovulation happen?
prompts.answer: About day 18, because 32 − 14 = 18. The fourteen days are counted back from the end of the cycle, so a longer cycle ovulates later.

prompts.prompt: Give two secondary sexual characteristics caused by testosterone and two caused by oestrogen.
prompts.answer: Testosterone: a deeper voice and the growth of facial hair. Oestrogen: the breasts develop and the hips widen.

prompts.prompt: What happens to the lining of the uterus if the ovum is not fertilised?
prompts.answer: The level of progesterone falls, so the lining is no longer maintained. It breaks down and is lost, which is menstruation, and day 1 of the next cycle begins.

prompts.prompt: On a hormone graph with no numbers on the vertical axis, what can you read and what can you not?
prompts.answer: You can read the timing: when each curve rises, peaks and falls. You cannot compare the heights of two different hormones, because the axis has no scale.
